speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Roseola Infantum (Exanthem Subitum)

The patient is an 11-year-old girl, which is older than the typical age range for Roseola (usually <2 years), but the clinical progression of a febrile prodrome followed by a rash that spares the perioral area is highly suggestive. Did the fever completely subside before the rash appeared?
